objects.why: Every unspent dollar, the Vanguard balance, the $130,000 left behind.
The save-save-save doctrine and the net worth that outlives its owner.
The richest corpse in the cemetery — dying rich as failure.
Inheritance given while it can still change a life, not mailed from the grave.
The $130,000 bequest that arrived at 49 instead of 30.
The biological clock on the currency — time buckets with expiry dates.
Go-go, slow-go, no-go years running out.
Pricing the fear of running out against the certainty of running out of time.
The peak net-worth date every saver should plan, not drift past.
The life journey and the deliberate drawdown curve toward zero.
The safety net, annuity and insurance — protection priced against living.
The healthspan wallet: knees, energy and the body that sets the exchange rate.
Memory dividends compounding — early experiences paying interest for decades.

spine.claim: Dying rich is not discipline but miscalculation: every dollar left at death is an experience refused while the body could still feel it.
Money buys lifetime fulfillment only inside health windows — memory dividends compound from early experiences, and every adventure carries a biological expiry date.
The net-worth curve should crest in middle age and deliberately fall toward zero; oversaving is fear insurance bought at an irrational markup.
Inheritance delayed is inheritance destroyed — money must move to children and causes while it can still change a life, and health itself is the wallet that sets the exchange rate.
Spend with audacity while youth, energy and health favor you, or admit at the grave that you hoarded tickets and never went to the carnival.
